fields.h1: Build a Song Request Form That Reaches Whoever Plays the Music
fields.hero_description: Build a song request form that puts every request in front of the DJ, band, or host and saves it to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Requests the Music Can Act On
fields.features_subheading: A song request form turns scattered asks at the booth into one list, and every request names a song and the artist who recorded it.
fields.feature_1:
Requests from a card on every table

Print the form's link as a QR code on each table card. Guests type the song title and the artist on their own phones and pick their table number, and nobody has to walk to the booth.
fields.feature_2:
Repeat requests count as votes

When a second guest asks for a song already on the list, the form adds a vote to that request instead of a new row. The songs the most guests asked for rise to the top of the queue.
fields.feature_3:
A live queue on the DJ's tablet

Requests show up on the DJ's tablet or laptop the moment a guest submits, with no refresh. Mark a song as played and it leaves the queue before a second guest asks for it again.
fields.feature_4:
Only songs from the band's set list

Load the songs a band knows, and the form offers them as a searchable list instead of a blank box. Guests choose a song the band can play, not one it never learned to play.
fields.feature_5:
A cutoff before the music is set

Close the form at a time you choose, like the start of the last set or 48 hours before a service. A request sent after the cutoff gets a note on screen or moves to the next show.
fields.feature_6:
Code that leaves with you

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and host it where you like. Every request sits in a database you own, and no response cap stops the form mid-party.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Asks for the Song, and Who Plays It
fields.tab_content_1:
By 9:00 PM, one song leads 31 requests

Every table at Crabapple Hill Barn has a QR card for Marguerite Ashby-Klein and Joaquin Pellerin's reception on Saturday, August 21, 2027. Guests send the song title, the artist, and their table number. By 9:00 PM, DJ Ruairi Okonjo-Vale of Mapleshade Sound has 31 requests, and a song 6 guests asked for leads the queue.
fields.tab_content_2:
Guests pick from 120 songs, all of them playable

The Tidewater Hum knows 120 songs, and on Thursdays at Ropewalk Taproom the request form lists those and no others. A guest picks one and adds a first name. Bandleader Delphine Okafor-Strand watches the list fill on a tablet by the mic stand. At 11:30 PM the last set starts, and the form stops taking requests.
fields.tab_content_3:
For Henrietta, 3 songs 48 hours before the service

Families at Cobbleford Funeral Home pick up to 3 songs and where each plays. For Ambrose Vennick's service on Saturday, March 13, 2027, his family picks an opening song, one after the eulogy, and a closing song. The form closes 48 hours before, and organist Henrietta Larkworthy gets the 3 by email, in order.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any request after 7:30 PM waits a week

Kettle Creek Community Radio runs a Friday request hour at 8:00 PM. Listeners send a song title, the artist, and a dedication of up to 140 characters. A request sent after 7:30 PM moves to next Friday. Host Ignatius Moreau-Bello opens 18 for Friday, April 16, 2027, starting with Marisela Duquesne's song for her father.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Song Request Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a song request form that gets each request to whoever plays the music, before a cutoff you set.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for the song before the name
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Match the choices to the set list
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the person who acts on each request: a DJ at a reception, a bandleader on stage, an organist, or a radio host. What that person needs in hand decides the fields, and where they read requests decides how each one reaches them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open the form with the song and its artist, the two answers the music depends on. Add a table number for a reception or a first name for a bar. Keep any dedication line optional so a request takes seconds to send.
fields.howto_step_3_des: If a band plays only what it has rehearsed, load that set list and offer it as a searchable dropdown. A DJ with a full library can leave the song field open and let guests type any title they like.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the cutoff: when the last set starts, two days before a service, or half an hour before a radio show. Then decide what a late request gets, a closing note on screen or a place in the next show's list.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the fields and the cutoff into one prompt. Emergent builds the song request form, the database behind it, and the screen the DJ or band reads. Ask in plain English when something needs to change later.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send a test request from the back row
fields.howto_step_6_des: Before the event, scan the QR code from the farthest table and send a request over mobile data. Send the same song a second time, then check that the DJ's tablet shows it once, with 2 votes.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Put the link where people will see it
fields.howto_step_7_des: Print the QR code on table cards, on the taproom's chalkboard, or in the program for a service. For a radio show, read a short link on air and post it on the station's site before the request hour opens.

faq_plan.q: What is a song request form?
faq_plan.a: A song request form is a short form that guests or listeners fill in to ask for a specific song. It records the requested song and its artist, plus who asked or where they sit, and passes the request to the musician or host on duty.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a song request form?
faq_plan.a: Decide who reads the requests, what each one must carry, and when requests stop. Describe that in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form, a database for the requests, and the queue screen, and you share the link or a QR code at the event.

faq_plan.q: What fields belong in a song request form template?
faq_plan.a: Start with two required fields, song and artist. A song request form template then adds a first name, a table number for a seated event, and an optional dedication. Keep it to five fields or fewer so a guest finishes in seconds. Emergent builds the same fields from a plain-English description, so the template is optional.

faq_plan.q: Should a song request form be separate from the form a client uses to book the music?
faq_plan.a: Yes, keep them apart. A DJ booking form is filled in once by the client, with the date, the venue, and the timeline. A song request form stays open during the event and takes many short requests from guests. Put the client's own must-play list on the booking side.

faq_plan.q: When should a song request form stop taking requests?
faq_plan.a: Stop it at the point the music can no longer change. For a band, close it when the final set begins. For a service, close it a day or two ahead so the musician can rehearse, and for a radio request hour, about 30 minutes before air. Show late senders when requests open again.

faq_plan.q: How should a song request form handle the same song requested twice?
faq_plan.a: Count each repeat as a vote on the first request instead of adding a new entry. Sort the queue by votes, and the DJ sees what the room wants without scrolling past duplicates. Match on the title and the artist together, since two songs can share a title. Emergent builds that matching rule from one sentence in the prompt.

faq_plan.q: Can a song request form be part of booking a private party?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add an optional song step at the end of the venue's booking form, with room for up to 10 songs and the artist of each. The requests then sit on the same record as the party's date and room, ready for whoever plays that night.

faq_plan.q: Should a song request form ask for a dedication?
faq_plan.a: Only where someone will read it aloud, such as a radio request hour or an anniversary party. Skip it on a busy dance floor. Keep the field optional and set a character limit, like 140, so the host can read each one on air in a single breath.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep the requests from a song request form after the event?
faq_plan.a: Save every request to a database instead of a group chat or paper slips. Afterward, the list shows which songs were asked for and how often, which helps plan the next playlist. Emergent builds the form with no response cap, and every request is saved to a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can a restaurant with live music use a song request form at the table?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Print a QR code for every table that opens the request form, and ask for the song, the artist, and the table number. Send the same link in the confirmation from the restaurant reservation form, and regulars can request a song before they arrive.

plan.angle: No live top 10 for this Wave 3 keyword, and every AlsoAsked question drifts to radio trivia or the most-requested song ever, so the page wins on what a working request form does that a paper slip or a generic template does not: requests that arrive with a table number, repeat requests counted as votes, a request list limited to songs the band can play, a cutoff before the music is set, and dedications for a radio request hour. Four real settings carry it: a wedding reception, a taproom cover band, a memorial service, and a community radio show. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, the template fields, how it differs from a DJ booking, cutoffs, repeat requests, private events, dedications, keeping requests in hand, and restaurants with live music.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Song Request Form That Reaches Whoever Plays the Music' and the hero cover the whole job, putting 'every request in front of the DJ, band, or host' and saving it to a database you own; slug song-request matches slug_for.

intent.evidence: Covers the template secondary with a field list ('Start with two required fields, song and artist ... Keep it to five fields or fewer'), plus a how-to, cutoffs, duplicates and dedications.

specificity.evidence: Speaks to DJs, bandleaders, organists and radio hosts in their own terms: 'when the last set starts', 'scan the QR code from the farthest table and send a request over mobile data'.

openers.evidence: Bodies open on full sentences: 'Print the form's link as a QR code on each table card.', 'The Tidewater Hum knows 120 songs'.

craft.evidence: Varied rhythm; two ', so' endings remain under the QC limit (recorded as a note).

voice.evidence: 'Slips at the booth get lost by the second set.' reads like a human operator; one muddled sentence in feature 3 is recorded as a note.

truth.evidence: Claims map to claims_used (realtime 'with no refresh', database-owned, alerts, no-caps, code-export, prompt-build). Weekdays check out (Sat Aug 21 2027, Sat Mar 13 2027, Fri Apr 16 2027), the cutoffs agree (48 hours / two days; 7:30 PM for an 8:00 PM hour = 'half an hour' / 'about 30 minutes'), the table comes from the library, and there are no third-party facts.

distinct.evidence: Has its own angle (repeat requests as votes, set-list-only choices, cutoffs). The DJ booking, booking and restaurant reservation forms appear only as links, and FAQ 4 separates the song request form from the booking form.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, each answered first ('Yes, keep them apart.', 'Stop it at the point the music can no longer change.'). No brand or format asks; the secondary 'song request form template' reads naturally in FAQ 3.

images.evidence: Tab 1 shows 31 requests, 'Lanterns on the Water' with 6 votes, Saturday, August 21, 2027 and DJ Ruairi Okonjo-Vale. Tab 2 shows 120 songs, first name Odile and 'Requests close at 11:30 PM'. Tab 3 shows Abide With Me / In the Garden / Amazing Grace emailed to Henrietta Larkworthy, 48 hours before. Tab 4 shows 18 requests, Friday, April 16, 2027, 'If sent after 7:30 PM -> next Friday' and Marisela's song for her father. Every tab matches its copy.
